- heading "Moonlight Philodendron Care" [level=2]
- paragraph:
  - strong: Light
  - text: ": Prefers bright, indirect light. Too much direct sunlight can fade the vibrant leaf colors, while insufficient light can lead to leggy growth. A spot near a window with a sheer curtain is ideal."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Soil
  - text: ": Thrives in well-draining, rich, organic soil. A mix of peat moss, perlite, and vermiculite provides the perfect balance for moisture retention and drainage."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Water
  - text: ": Water when the top inch of soil feels dry. Moonlight Philodendron enjoys consistent moisture but is prone to root rot in overly wet conditions. Ensure the pot has good drainage."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Temperature and Humidity
  - text: ": Prefers warm temperatures between 65°F (18°C) and 85°F (29°C). Protect it from cold drafts and sudden temperature drops to avoid stress. Prefers higher humidity levels, around 60-80%. Use a humidifier, mist the plant regularly, or place it on a pebble tray with water to increase ambient humidity, mimicking its tropical habitat."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Fertilization
  - text: ": Fertilize every 4-6 weeks during the growing season (spring and summer) with a balanced, liquid fertilizer diluted to half the recommended strength. Reduce fertilization in fall and winter."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Pruning
  - text: ": Prune any yellow or damaged leaves to encourage healthy growth. Pruning can also help maintain the plant’s shape and promote fuller growth."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Repotting
  - text: ": Repot every 2-3 years or when the plant becomes root-bound. Choose a pot only slightly larger than the previous one to prevent excess soil moisture."

- paragraph: Philodendrons can encounter pests, diseases, and other common problems, especially when grown indoors.
- heading "Pests" [level=3]
- paragraph:
  - link "Spider Mites":
    - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/pest/spider-mites
    - strong: Spider Mites
  - text: ": These tiny pests can be identified by the fine webs they weave on the plant. They cause yellowing or speckled leaves. Increase humidity around the plant and wash it with a strong stream of water. For severe infestations, use insecticidal soap or neem oil."
- paragraph:
  - strong:
    - link "Mealybugs":
      - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/pest/mealybugs
    - text: ":"
  - text: These white, cottony pests tend to cluster in leaf axils and under leaves, sucking sap and weakening the plant. Remove with alcohol-dipped cotton swabs or apply
  - link "neem oil":
    - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/guide/neem-oil-for-plants-how-to-use-this-organic-insecticide
    - strong: neem oil
  - text: .
- paragraph:
  - strong:
    - link "Aphids":
      - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/pest/aphids
    - text: ":"
  - text: Small, soft-bodied insects that can be green, black, brown, or pink, aphids typically feed in groups on the undersides of leaves. Combat them with a gentle spray of water,
  - link "neem oil":
    - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/guide/neem-oil-for-plants-how-to-use-this-organic-insecticide
    - strong: neem oil
  - text: ", or insecticidal soap to protect the plant’s health and appearance."
- paragraph:
  - strong:
    - link "Scale insects":
      - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/pest/scale-insects
    - text: ":"
  - text: Hard or soft-bodied insects that attach themselves to the stems or leaves, causing yellowing and growth stunting. Scrape off with a fingernail or use a cotton swab dipped in rubbing alcohol. Insecticidal soap or
  - link "neem oil":
    - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/guide/neem-oil-for-plants-how-to-use-this-organic-insecticide
    - strong: neem oil
  - text: may also be used.
- heading "Diseases" [level=3]:
  - generic: Diseases
- paragraph:
  - strong:
    - link "Root rot":
      - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/disease/root-rot
    - text: ":"
  - text: Overwatering is the primary cause, leading to brown, mushy roots and yellowing leaves. Reduce watering, improve drainage, and repot the plant into fresh, well-draining soil. Severely affected roots should be trimmed before repotting.
- paragraph:
  - link "Leaf spot":
    - /url: https://www.gardenia.net/disease/leaf-spot-diseases
    - strong: Leaf spot
  - text: ": Fungal or bacterial infections can cause dark or black spots on leaves, often with a yellow halo. Increase air circulation, avoid wetting leaves when watering, and remove affected leaves. Fungicides or bactericides may be necessary in severe cases."
- heading "Common Problems" [level=3]
- paragraph:
  - strong: Yellowing Leaves
  - text: ": Often a sign of overwatering or poor drainage. Ensure the plant is in well-draining soil and adjust your watering schedule to allow the soil to dry slightly between waterings."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Brown Leaf Tips
  - text: ": Can indicate low humidity, especially in dry indoor environments. Increase humidity around the plant with a humidifier, pebble tray, or by misting the leaves regularly."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Leaf Scorch
  - text: ": Direct sunlight can cause the leaves to scorch, leading to brown patches or fading of the vibrant leaf colors. Position the plant in a location where it receives bright, indirect light."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Drooping Leaves
  - text: ": This can be a sign of both underwatering and overwatering. Check the soil moisture to determine the cause and adjust your watering accordingly."
- paragraph:
  - strong: Slow Growth or Lack of Color
  - text: ": Insufficient light can lead to less vibrant leaf coloration and slow growth. Ensure your philodendron is receiving enough indirect light to maintain its rich hues and promote healthy growth."
